summary: Epigenetic reprogramming of T cells into antigen-specific regulatory cells for immune tolerance.
editor_note: Reprogramming pathogenic T cells is a sharper proposition than suppressing the whole immune system. The platform aims to create stable, antigen-specific regulatory cells without gene engineering, supported by published preclinical work. The financing separates $44M of Series A equity from roughly $22M of grants. Human safety, manufacturing consistency and lasting immune tolerance remain the decisive tests.
investors: Playground Global, Global Brain, Mitsui Chemicals, LG Technology Ventures, Alumni Ventures, Medical Incubator Japan, Fast Track Initiative, The University of Tokyo Edge Capital Partners, Osaka University Venture Capital, Kyoto iCAP

sources.label: RegCell via Business Wire funding announcement

product_evidence.claim: The platform describes epigenetic conversion of pathogenic T cells into stable antigen-specific regulatory T cells without genetic engineering.
The publication announcement describes preclinical mouse inflammatory-disease models and human patient-derived cells, not human clinical efficacy.

market_context.primary_user: Cell-therapy researchers pursuing antigen-specific treatments for autoimmune disease.
market_context.differentiation: Uses epigenetic reprogramming and antigen specificity instead of generalized immunosuppression or gene engineering.
market_context.why_now: Equity and separately identified grants support clinical translation of a published preclinical platform.

risks.claim: Preclinical immune control may not become safe and durable human benefit.
risks.basis: Inspected evidence describes animal models and patient-derived cells; clinical development remains ahead.
